name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks. This lets us measure real-world impact without risking bad changes. The trade-off is slower feedback loops—we won’t see improvements immediately—but we avoid breaking builds or annoying teams with noisy suggestions. After two weeks, we’ll have data to decide if PR-Agent adds enough value to enable it fully.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode won’t catch PR-Agent’s worst flaw: false negatives. It normalizes them as "acceptable" because it never forces a change—teams still miss real issues. Instead, run PR-Agent in *parallel mode* on a strict subset of PRs (e.g., low-risk changes only) for two weeks, then compare its false negative rate to manual reviews. If it misses fewer than 5% more than humans, we auto-apply safe suggestions; if not, we scrap it.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in parallel mode on *new contributors’ PRs only*—they’re less likely to have deep context, so false negatives hurt more there. This cuts the test scope to ~20% of PRs, saving compute and time while still catching the highest-value misses.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in parallel mode on new contributors’ PRs only for two weeks. This targets the highest-risk false negatives where context gaps hurt most, cutting scope to ~20% of PRs without wasting compute on veteran PRs. The trade-off is delayed visibility into false positives on core contributor PRs—we’ll miss some noise but catch the critical misses early. After two weeks, we’ll have clean data to decide whether to expand or adjust.
